articles.title: GBP/USD starts the week on a strong footing
articles.expand: GBP/USD enters the week of 10–14 August near 1.3500 – its highest level since 15 July. Sterling is building on the momentum from a sharp decline in the dollar following a weak US labour market report, which reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September.

articles.title: Euro: Fed repricing supports gains against US Dollar – Societe Generale
articles.expand: Societe Generale strategists highlight that EUR/USD has squeezed above key resistance as Dollar weakness follows softer United States (US) employment data and reduced odds of a September Fed hike. The pair is seen slightly expensive versus nat gas but near fair value on 2-year spreads.

articles.title: Gold Hovers Near Seven-week High As Fed Hike Bets Ease
articles.expand: (RTTNews) - Gold prices held steady on Monday after U.S. employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July and hiring figures for the prior two months were also revised downward, helping ease the risk of an immediate U.S. interest-rate hike.

articles.title: Australian Dollar: Hawkish RBA hold supports carry – BBH
articles.expand: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that the Australian Dollar (AUD) remains one of the most attractive G10 currencies thanks to favorable carry and a hawkish Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

articles.title: Canadian Dollar: Recovery against US Dollar faces tariff risks – Commerzbank
articles.expand: Michael Pfister at Commerzbank highlights a strong Canadian labour market and improving Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and exports as signs of real-economy recovery, but warns this is fragile due to threatened US tariffs.

articles.title: Brent: Iran talks keep risk premium in focus – Deutsche Bank

articles.title: The commodities feed: Oil higher as supply risks persist
articles.expand: Oil prices remain supported by ongoing uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, speculative sentiment has turned more cautious, with money managers reducing net long positions in both NYMEX WTI and ICE Brent.

articles.expand: A weak jobs report already made the case for a Fed hold, but only Wednesday's CPI can confirm inflation is cooling too — and if it comes in soft without reviving growth fears, Silver's dual identity as both a monetary and industrial metal could let it outrun Gold. articles.title: RBA preview: Hawkish hold widely expected; traders attentive to potential dovish surprises

The central bank will also release the SMP at this meeting with updated macroeconomic forecasts where inflation is expected to be revised lower and the unemployment rate higher. articles.expand: The USDCAD has been trading within well-defined ranges since peaking at the end of June. The first "box" was established between 1.41297 and 1.4243. Price action inside both ranges has been relatively orderly, with the 100-hour and 200-hour moving averages serving as a reliable barometer of short-term control. articles.title: Eurozone Retail Sales Fall Unexpectedly
articles.expand: Eurozone retail sales declined unexpectedly in June after rising moderately in May, suggesting a meagre contribution by consumption to economic growth, official data revealed Thursday. Retail sales decreased 0.3 percent in June from May, Eurostat reported. Sales had increased 0.4 percent in May but fell 0.4 percent in April.
